messages:
morgan: Quick question — we're debating two patterns for private VPC egress resiliency for tenant traffic: 1) mirror egress to a secondary region (tap/copy) for passive warm standby, or 2) active-passive failover where we switch endpoint routing to a healthy region. Thoughts on tradeoffs? :thinking:

lia: tl;dr: mirroring preserves session visibility but doesn't solve source IP preservation or TCP failover; active-passive gives better single-request recovery if switch is atomic, but is riskier for long lived connections.

sam: Agree with lia. Also mirror option bloats egress bandwidth and doubles cost for sensitive customers. Mirroring is great for replay/debugging and shadowing rollout, not for production failover imo.

nora: Some specifics we hit before: if we mirror at the NAT/relay level we still SNAT -> loses src ip. To preserve src IP you need L3 handoff (e.g., ENI move / duplicate routes) which is much heavier and touches customer's VPC architecture.

ben: One more infra constraint: our PrivateEndpoint service in region-A advertises private DNS + route to tenant. For active-passive we can flip the DNS TTL and fail traffic to region-B, but existing TCP connections will 1) keep trying 2) potentially hit half-open backends. Clients that use connection pooling will see errors.

morgan: Good flags. What about a hybrid: mirror traffic to region-B for warm caches + health-check based pre-warm, then on failover perform a coordinated cutover (DNS TTL + route withdraw) with a short blackout window?

lia: That hybrid is promising. Playbook sketch: 1) continuously mirror non-sensitive headers/prefixes to warm pool in region-B; 2) run active health probes from both regions; 3) on failover do: withdraw route/endpoint in region-A -> announce in region-B -> update DNS + API fallback; 4) Post-cutover reconciliation + replay missing messages from mirror logs.

sam: Operational notes: need to ensure our mirror does NOT copy PII by default — strip payloads or sample. Also add traffic budget alarms: if mirror bandwidth > X% of baseline, auto-throttle.

nora: For the route flip we might use BGP prepends from region-A to influence path before full withdraw. Example prepends we used in spike: ```
# on edge-router
neighbor 10.1.1.1 route-map PREPEND out
route-map PREPEND permit 10
set as-path prepend 65000 65000
```
Helps drain gracefully.

ben: How does this affect Dedicated customers with pinned endpoints? They expect IP stability. Active-passive DNS flip breaks that. Mirroring preserves their endpoint IPs but won't help if the underlying compute is down. We need separate contract for pinned-IP SLAs.

morgan: Good point. So recommended patterns per class: - Self-serve tenants: hybrid mirror + DNS failover (short TTL) - Dedicated/pinned IP: require cross-region reserved IP bridging or manual migration playbook + scheduled maintenance windows.

deploy-bot: Reminder: we have an existing canary that mirrors 5% of traffic to eu-west-2 for 24h -> logs show 1.7x egress cost on that slice.

lia: Action items: 1) draft a cutover playbook doc with exact TTLs, expected client behavior, rollback steps; 2) add mirror sampling & payload redaction in the proxy; 3) product: update Dedicated contracts + migration options page.

sam: I'll prototype a small test that does mirror+pre-warm caches and measure latencies + cold cache miss rate. Putting notes in the spike doc. :+1:

morgan: Thanks all — I'll spin up the cutover playbook draft and ping @lia for review. If anyone has hard constraints from customers (pinned IP or data residency) drop them here or DM me.
